titleText.es: Letra pequeña: este horario volverá loco de remate a cualquiera.
titleText.en: Small print: this schedule will eventually drive one stark raving mad.
titleText.noteEn: Loco de remate is an emphatic expression for being completely or stark raving mad.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: After tener problemas, para can introduce the action that is difficult for someone. In natural English, tener problemas para dormir means “to have trouble sleeping,” not “to have problems in order to sleep.”
Unaccented como can introduce the person, thing, or situation used for a comparison. It does not ask “how”; the question word cómo has an accent.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: tener problemas para + verbo en forma de diccionario
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone has trouble doing an action?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of tener problemas para, then the unchanged action verb.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Only tener changes for the person and time. The action after para stays in its dictionary form ending in -ar, -er, or -ir. Natural English often uses “have trouble” followed by an -ing form.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: right?; isn't that so? (at the end of a question)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After a statement or assumption, ¿no? asks the listener to confirm it. English often uses a changing tag such as “right?”, “isn't it?”, or “don't you?”, but Spanish can use the same ¿no? after many different verbs.
Terminado is the completed-action form of terminar, “to finish.” After a form of haber such as ha, it stays unchanged rather than matching the person or thing that finished.
Como can mean “because” when it introduces the reason before the main point. If the reason follows the main point, porque is usually the more natural connector.

example.en: Since it is raining, we will go by bus.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Deberías is the advice form of deber for one familiar listener. It softens the statement into a recommendation rather than saying what the listener absolutely must do.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: debería/deberías… + verbo en forma de diccionario
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone should do something?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use an advice form of deber, then keep the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The dictionary form is the unchanged verb ending in -ar, -er, or -ir. Use debería for “I,” “he,” “she,” or formal “you,” deberías for one familiar “you,” deberíamos for “we,” and deberían for a plural subject. The following action verb does not change.
Dormido comes from dormir, “to sleep.” As a description of a person or animal, it means that the subject is asleep; dormida is used for a feminine singular subject.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you introduce a real or possible condition with “if”?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use si without an accent, followed by an ordinary present-time verb form.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: This pattern treats the condition as genuinely possible. Spanish normally does not put a future-tense verb directly after si in this kind of condition; the result can appear separately as a statement, prediction, or command.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; marks ajustarse, “to fit or adapt”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ajustarse uses a short marker such as me, te, se, or nos when the subject itself fits or adapts. Without that marker, ajustar more often means adjusting something else.

example.es: El plan se ajusta al presupuesto.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ajusta is the present form used with one other person or thing. With se and a, it describes that subject fitting, matching, or adapting to something.

example.es: La tapa se ajusta a la caja.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to; required before what something fits or adapts to
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ajustarse requires a before the standard, situation, or thing that the subject fits or adapts to.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something fits, matches, or adapts to something else?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of ajustarse, then a before the thing it fits or adapts to.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The short marker changes with the subject: me ajusto, te ajustas, se ajusta, nos ajustamos, and so on. The form of ajustar also changes for the person and time, while a remains before the comparison or situation.

example.es: La propuesta se ajusta a las reglas.
example.en: The proposal conforms to the rules.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pasar often means “to pass” or “to go by.” With a period or amount of time, it can instead describe how someone spends that time.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: working; work (in días laborales, workdays or weekdays)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Laborales describes things connected with work. Días laborales are the days normally treated as workdays, in contrast with the weekend.

example.es: La oficina abre los días laborales.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can you express “in a ... way” by using forma?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use de forma, then an adjective that describes that way of doing something.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Forma is a feminine noun, so an adjective with separate masculine and feminine forms uses its feminine form here: clara, rápida, cuidadosa. Adjectives such as normal that have one form for both genders do not change.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to go out (socially or for entertainment)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Salir can mean simply leaving a place, but it also commonly means going out to socialize, eat, drink, dance, or enjoy entertainment.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: just like; the same as (with que)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Igual normally means “equal” or “the same.” Followed by que and a comparison, it works as the common connector igual que, “just like” or “the same as.”
After igual, que introduces the person or thing used as the comparison. The two words form the connector igual que.

example.en: It is the same as the original.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone or something is like another person or thing in the same way?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use igual que before the person or thing being used for comparison.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The connector means “just like” or “the same as.” Igual stays unchanged in this connector, and que introduces the reference point for the comparison.
Suponer can mean “to suppose,” but it also describes the result, amount, or consequence that something represents.

example.es: El cambio supone una hora más.
example.en: The change means one extra hour.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Before a unit of time, por can distribute an amount across each unit, corresponding to English “per” or “a”: por día, por semana, por noche.

example.en: I read one hour per day.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pasar often means “to pass,” but with an amount or period of time it can describe spending that time in an activity, place, or state.

example.en: I want to spend an hour reading.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Haciéndolo joins haciendo, the ongoing-action form of hacer, to lo, “it.” The written accent keeps the original stress in the same place after lo is attached.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you attach a word such as “it,” “him,” “her,” or “them” to an ongoing-action form?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Join lo, la, los, las, or another object marker to the end of the verb's -ando or -iendo form, adding a written accent when needed to preserve the original stress.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The -ando or -iendo form, often called a gerund, presents an action in progress or alongside another action. An object marker can follow it as one written word: haciendo becomes haciéndolo, and leyendo becomes leyéndola. The accent shows that the stressed syllable has not shifted after the extra syllable is added.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: you; identifies the person being estimated
cardDefinitions.noteEn: With echar in its estimating sense, te points to the familiar listener whose age, time, or other amount the speaker is estimating.

example.en: I estimate you at about twenty years old.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Echo is the present form of echar for the speaker. Echar has many meanings; before an approximate age, time, or amount, it can mean “to estimate.” Echo has no h, unlike hecho, “done” or “made.”

example.en: I estimate that person to be about thirty.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can echar mean that you estimate someone's age, time, or another amount?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use me, te, le, nos, or les with a form of echar, then give the approximate quantity.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The short object marker identifies the person or thing being estimated, while echar changes for the speaker and time. This estimating sense is different from the basic meaning “to throw”; it is common with ages, durations, distances, and similar quantities.

example.en: I estimate that person to be about thirty.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Bien evaluates the manner or result of an action. In bien jugado, it praises a clever move, joke, or comeback.
Jugado is the completed-action form of jugar, “to play.” In the reaction bien jugado, the idea extends from games to any clever move or reply.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: What can you say after someone makes a clever move, joke, or comeback?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The expression comes from praising a move in a game, but it is also used figuratively to acknowledge that someone handled a situation cleverly or delivered an effective reply.

example.en: It was a trick. Well played.

applications.explanationEn: Tienes matches the familiar listener, problemas names the difficulty, and para introduces the difficult action dormir rather than a purpose.

regions.labelEs: SÓLO CUANDO HA TERMINADO TU MADRE.

applications.explanationEn: Ha is the present helper used with one other person, and terminado is the unchanged completed-action form.

regions.labelEs: ...DEBERÍAS PROBAR EL DÍA DE 28 HORAS. 20 DESPIERTO, 8 DORMIDO. (O 19/9, SI PREFIERES).

excludedUnits.rationale: This numeral states the proposed day's length and is not a Spanish lexical word.
This numeral states the hours awake and is not a Spanish lexical word.
This numeral states the hours asleep and is not a Spanish lexical word.
This slash-separated pair gives alternative awake and asleep hour measurements rather than Spanish vocabulary.

applications.explanationEn: Deberías addresses one familiar listener with advice, and probar stays in its unchanged dictionary form.
Si introduces the optional condition, and prefieres uses the ordinary present form for one familiar listener.
A appears before the specific person identified by tu madre because that person directly receives the action of prefiero.

regions.labelEs: SE AJUSTA A LA SEMANA... PASAS LOS DÍAS LABORALES DESPIERTO DE FORMA NORMAL, Y LOS FINES DE SEMANA PUEDES SALIR TODA LA NOCHE.

applications.explanationEn: Se marks that the subject itself fits, ajusta is the one-thing present form, and a introduces la semana as the standard it fits.
De forma introduces a manner, and normal describes forma without changing because normal has the same form with masculine and feminine nouns.
Fines is the plural of fin, while de semana stays unchanged in the standard expression for multiple weekends.
Puedes carries the familiar-you form of ability, and salir stays in its unchanged dictionary form.
Igual que forms the comparison connector, and tu madre supplies the person used as its reference point.

regions.labelEs: SUPONE CUATRO HORAS MÁS POR DÍA. ¡PUEDES ESTAR DESPIERTO HASTA LA EXTENUACIÓN TODOS LOS DÍAS Y LUEGO PASAR 9 HORAS COMPLETAS DORMIDO POR NOCHE!

excludedUnits.rationale: This numeral states the number of sleeping hours and is not a Spanish lexical word.

applications.explanationEn: Puedes carries the familiar-you form of ability, and estar remains in its unchanged dictionary form.

regions.labelEs: ¿PERO CUÁNTO TIEMPO PUEDO PASAR HACIÉNDOLO CON TU MADRE?

applications.explanationEn: Puedo carries the speaker's form of ability, and pasar stays in its unchanged dictionary form.
Lo is joined to haciendo, and the written accent preserves the original stress after the extra syllable is attached.

regions.labelEs: ¿TÚ? YO TE ECHO TRES O CUATRO MINUTOS.

applications.exampleEs: TE ECHO TRES O CUATRO MINUTOS
applications.explanationEn: Te marks the person being estimated, echo is the speaker's present form of echar, and tres o cuatro minutos supplies the approximate quantity.
Bien evaluates how the move was made, and jugado supplies the game-derived wording of this conventional reaction.
